newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal ex-president heads gold probe commission.
newsitem.headline: Portugal ex-president heads gold probe commission.

text.p: Former Portuguese president Mario Soares will head a special commission helping probe gold Portugal received from Nazi Germany during World War Two, the country's central bank said on Thursday.

The three-man commission, to include a representative of the Jewish community, will accompany the work of economic historian Joaquim Costa Leite, appointed last December by the Bank of Portugal to investigate its gold dealings in the years 1937-46.
Portugal was the second largest buyer of gold from Nazi Germany after Switzerland during World War Two giving rise to suspicions some of the bullion bought was looted.

Nazi troops removed bullion from countries invaded during the war, including Belgium and Holland, and there is also the highly emotive question of what happened to gold -- watches, jewellry and even teeth -- stolen from concentration camp victims.

Portugal, which was ruled by a right-wing dictatorship at the time, says that the gold acquired during the war years was in payment for exports it was legally allowed to make as an officially neutral country to Germany and its allies.
The Bank of Portugal said that the names of the other two commissioners would be announced next month.
